title: Care for health over time without a doctor
short: Examining the sick, medicines, chronic illness, teeth, pregnancy, mental health, disability
intro: A beginner's path for looking after a household's health for weeks or months when doctors, pharmacies and clinics are hard to reach. It starts with how to use the main village-health books and moves on to medicines, long-term conditions, teeth, pregnancy, stress and caring for people with disabilities. Knowing when to get skilled help is part of every step.

limits.text: Part of informed self-care is knowing your limits: the book points out when to see or get advice from a health worker or doctor.

A person with one or more signs of dangerous illness (such as heavy blood loss, coughing blood, cannot be woken, no urine for 12 hours, high fever that won't come down) is probably too sick to treat at home: seek skilled medical help as soon as possible.
Never use a dangerous medicine for a mild illness. Use medicines only when necessary, use the right dose, stop if it causes problems, and ask a health worker when in doubt.
Expired medicines can be dangerous, some (such as tetracyclines) especially so; keep all medicines out of reach of children because any medicine in large doses can be poisonous.
MSF Essential Drugs is a practical manual intended for physicians, pharmacists, nurses and health auxiliaries, not for self-treatment.
MSF Clinical Guidelines are designed for medical professionals in curative care at dispensaries and primary hospitals.

Very high blood pressure with headache, blurred vision, chest pain, shortness of breath or seizures can be an emergency: take the person to a clinic or hospital. Lowering blood pressure too quickly can cause harm.
Do not just stop blood pressure medicine because of side effects; ask a health worker about another medicine. Stop and talk to a health worker if a rash or swelling appears.
A person with signs of very high blood sugar (severe thirst, extreme weakness or confusion, weight loss) should be tested and treated fast; very high blood sugar can kill.
Dental workers must know their limits and do only what they know how to do; some problems are too serious and should go to a more experienced dental worker.

Severe hemorrhage, eclampsia or a prolapsed cord cannot be treated at home. Procedures in A Book for Midwives that you have not been trained to do should be learned from someone experienced, not from reading.
Labor danger signs (very long labor, blood pressure 160/110 or higher, fever with fast pulse, sideways baby, cord coming first) need medical help.
If someone talks about suicide or death, take it seriously and ask directly; you do not have to help them alone – involve others and connect them with care.
Psychological first aid is delivered by people who have received appropriate training; it does not require professional mental health qualifications.
If someone behaves unusually aggressively or strangely, consider that it may be a physical health emergency; your own safety comes first in any crisis.
